definitions.explanation: The practice of hiring someone again, especially rehiring an employee after mandatory retirement. In Japan, this commonly refers to programs that allow employees to continue working past the official retirement age, typically under different contract terms.

examples.japanese: {定年|ていねん}{後|ご}に{再雇用|さいこよう}される。
examples.english: To be re-employed after mandatory retirement.

examples.japanese: {再雇用|さいこよう}{制度|せいど}を{利用|りよう}して{働|はたら}き{続|つづ}ける{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: More people are continuing to work by using the re-employment system.

examples.japanese: {再雇用|さいこよう}では{給与|きゅうよ}が{下|さ}がることが{多|おお}いが、{経験|けいけん}を{活|い}かせる{職場|しょくば}で{働|はたら}けるメリットがある。
examples.english: Although salary often decreases with re-employment, there is the advantage of working in a place where one can use their experience.

notes:
Compound noun: {再|さい} (again) + {雇用|こよう} (employment). Commonly used with する as a suru-verb.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {再雇用|さいこよう}{制度|せいど} (re-employment system)
- {再雇用|さいこよう}される (to be re-employed)
- {再雇用|さいこよう}{契約|けいやく} (re-employment contract)

CULTURE:
As Japan's population ages, {再雇用|さいこよう} programs have become increasingly important. Many companies offer re-employment to employees who have reached mandatory retirement age, allowing them to continue working — often with reduced hours and pay — until age 65 or beyond.
